     9	
    10	# Effect Patterns
    11	
    12	## Codex Provider Boundaries
    13	
    14	For the Codex subscription path, canonical schemas, tagged errors, Context
    15	services, explicit Layers, `Config`/`Redacted`, scoped loopback resources,
    16	native `KeyValueStore` composition, refresh locking, and fenced commits remain
    17	package-owned in `@bundjil/codex`; provider-neutral persistence contracts
    18	and adapters belong to `@bundjil/store`. `apps/codex-proxy` owns
    19	only app config and private HTTP composition. Do not recreate profile DTOs,
    20	token mappers, or OAuth routes in either app; Vercel must not host browser OAuth
    21	or account linking.
    22	
    23	Bundjil uses Effect for code that can fail, cross an async boundary, depend on
    24	runtime services, read configuration, or form a durable integration contract.
    25	Plain TypeScript is still fine for simple framework glue and local rendering,
    26	but package and boundary code should stay in the Effect model.
    27	
    28	This guide applies Bundjil's Effect service rules to its smaller Eve-first repo
    29	shape.
    30	
    31	## Default Rule
    32	
    33	Use Effect-native primitives first when working in packages, tools, app
    34	runtime config, or provider boundaries:
    35	
    36	- `Schema` for payloads, config values, tool inputs, tool outputs, and domain
    37	  contracts.
    38	- `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` or `Data.TaggedError` for expected failures.
    39	- `Context.Service` and `Layer` for dependency-injected operations.
    40	- `Config` and `ConfigProvider` for runtime config.
    41	- Object-form `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })` for Promise or SDK calls,
    42	  with rejection mapped at the owning boundary.
    43	- `Effect.all`, `Effect.race`, fibers, and other Effect primitives for owned
    44	  concurrency. Raw `Promise.all` and `Promise.race` are forbidden in production
    45	  app/package source even inside a `tryPromise` callback.
    46	- `Clock.currentTimeMillis`, `Effect.sleep`, schedules, and timeouts for
    47	  runtime time so `TestClock` can control Effect-owned tests.
    48	- `Effect.fn("Owner.operation")` for reusable semantic operations that own a
    49	  readable trace. Use `Effect.fnUntraced` only for a small leaf or public
    50	  service accessor whose invoked service operation already owns the trace.
    51	  Direct exported functions that construct `Effect.gen` are forbidden;
    52	  top-level Effect programs and local one-use generators remain valid.
    53	- `Match`, `Result`, and `Exit` for tagged branching and program outcomes.
    54	- Effect collection modules such as `Chunk`, `HashMap`, and `HashSet` when
    55	  persistent concatenation, Effect equality/hash, typed lookup absence, or
    56	  set algebra materially carries the domain. Ordinary immutable arrays,
    57	  records, and local native collections remain valid when those semantics do
    58	  not apply. A native `Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, or `WeakSet` constructor in owned
    59	  app/package source requires an exact occurrence-checked lint exception that
    60	  names its local algorithm, ordered diagnostic, host, or test-backend owner.
    61	
    62	Do not introduce Zod, local DTO mirrors, raw `unknown` readers, or hand-written
    63	success/error unions when an owning Effect Schema or tagged error can express
    64	the contract.
    65	
    66	## Service Shape
    67	
    68	An exported operation must make trace ownership visible at its declaration.
    69	Use a named `Effect.fn` when the operation performs policy, validation,
    70	orchestration, or other work whose failures need their own span. Use
    71	`Effect.fnUntraced` when a stable public accessor only acquires a service and
    72	delegates to an already named service operation; give its generator a useful
    73	function name for diagnostics. Do not add a pass-through accessor merely to
    74	rename a service method: it needs an existing public-package consumer or
    75	another concrete API-boundary reason. This distinction follows installed
    76	`effect@4.0.0-beta.101`; the reviewed v4 source revision is
    77	`1caab3cc30f626efbf15e59d74f539a487e5c85c`.
    78	
    79	Use this file layout when a package grows past one or two operations:
    80	
    81	```text
    82	src/
    83	  schemas.ts        canonical Effect Schema contracts and derived types
    84	  errors.ts         tagged error unions and public error exports
    85	  service.ts        Context.Service tag and public operation API
    86	  live.layer.ts     production layer and provider wiring
    87	  mock.layer.ts     deterministic layer for tests
    88	  index.ts          stable package contract
    89	```
    90	
    91	Bundjil currently keeps the small `@bundjil/eve` service in
    92	`src/services/workspace-operations.ts`. Split to the layout above when new
    93	operations or providers make the combined file harder to scan.
    94	
    95	Root `index.ts` should export stable contracts and default operation helpers.
    96	Implementation layers can be exported from the root while the package is small,
    97	but provider-heavy packages should eventually expose live/mock layers from
    98	explicit subpaths so callers choose the implementation deliberately.
    99	
   100	## Provider And SDK Client Boundaries
   101	
   102	A provider wrapper is a named adapter, not a general SDK capability. Its public
   103	service exposes owner-specific operations and only Schema-derived decoded
   104	inputs and outputs. The SDK instance, Promise API, raw failure, provider DTO,
   105	and any unavoidable primitive remain private to `*.live.layer.ts` or the exact
   106	owner adapter. A generic callback operation or exported raw client defeats the
   107	boundary and is forbidden.
   108	
   109	For every operation:
   110	
   111	1. Accept the canonical domain codec's `typeof Contract.Type`, including
   112	   owner-branded identifiers rather than raw semantic strings.
   113	2. Encode the outbound provider request with `Schema.encodeEffect` or the
   114	   framework-native `HttpClient` Schema body API immediately before the call.
   115	   Keep `typeof Contract.Encoded` inside the adapter.
   116	3. Wrap only the Promise call with object-form
   117	   `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })` and map raw failure once to an
   118	   owner-named, safe `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` failure.
   119	4. Decode the complete provider response immediately with
   120	   `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect`; use `Schema.decodeEffect` instead when the SDK
   121	   statically returns the codec's `Encoded` type.
   122	5. Return only the decoded domain result. Never return an unconstrained generic
   123	   or provider-owned response type.
   124	
   125	Semantic config uses `Config.schema`; secrets use owner-named redacted Schemas
   126	and are revealed only at immediate SDK construction or header assignment.
   127	Tests use a scoped `ConfigProvider` when proving configuration and a
   128	deterministic mock/memory Layer for service behavior. Every provider service
   129	exports explicit live and mock/memory Layers.
   130	
   131	When one provider service needs credentials selected by an already-decoded
   132	resource identity, expose a named semantic lookup over a Schema-owned tagged
   133	scope and return a closed safe error. Decode the complete credential set once
   134	inside the live operation, store it in Effect `HashMap` when keyed lookup is
   135	the domain operation, and fail on duplicate, unavailable, or unadmitted scope.
   136	Do not expose a raw Config effect as the service, accept primitive project IDs,
   137	or select credentials from their encoded wire representation. Keep broader
   138	inventory credentials and exact-resource automation credentials in distinct
   139	Layers when their authority differs.
   140	
   141	Compose dynamic already-decoded redacted config with the owning Schema's
   142	`.makeEffect` constructor so Type-side validation stays in the typed error
   143	channel; reserve `.make` for trusted static construction. Do not call
   144	`Redacted.value` merely to feed the
   145	plaintext into `Schema.decodeEffect` or `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` and create
   146	another redacted wrapper. `redacted-schema-roundtrip` enforces this while
   147	preserving immediate boundary reveals. When an external representation really
   148	must change, encode the owning redacted Schema at that exact egress before
   149	decoding the target wire/crypto representation; do not reveal and re-wrap it as
   150	an internal shortcut.
   151	
   152	Alchemy custom providers follow the same boundary. `Resource` props and
   153	attributes are canonical decoded Schema types; `Provider.succeed` delegates
   154	named `read`/`diff`/`reconcile`/`delete`/`list` operations to injected services
   155	and exposes no provider client. Reconciliation is observe-first and idempotent,
   156	adoption requires an exact reviewed metadata digest, uncertain writes recover
   157	by stable physical identity with bounded readback, and native Alchemy `sync`
   158	remains the drift engine. Provider credentials remain lazy `Context.Service`
   159	Effects backed by `Config.schema` and `Redacted` so Layer construction performs
   160	no credential read.
   161	
   162	Report-only drift wraps that native engine rather than remapping provider
   163	state through a parallel service. The adapter decodes the native desired plan
   164	and sync result once, fingerprints physical identities before persistence,
   165	classifies each observation through `Match`, and encodes only its owned report
   166	and bounded receipt at the file boundary. Native fields that do not expose
   167	attempts or duration stay explicitly `NotExposed`; missing observation data is
   168	not invented. The protected environment supplies a static, fingerprinted
   169	read-only policy artifact; it is not misrepresented as one-run identity. Each
   170	execution separately decodes a branded GitHub repository/run/attempt identity,
   171	the checked-out source SHA, and the already-decoded adoption-manifest digest,
   172	then carries all three through the report and receipt. A source-only actor or
   173	an unbound manifest is not accepted as hosted execution evidence.
   174	
   175	The Vercel read/import boundary applies this per operation: encode one
   176	owner-qualified request immediately before team/project/query assignment,
   177	decode the complete status/header/body envelope immediately after
   178	`HttpClient`, and map the private provider DTO once to a state-safe observation
   179	or list result. Every collection exhausts pagination. Sensitive environment
   180	observations contain metadata and an explicit sensitivity flag, never the
   181	value. Read/import reconcile re-observes without a provider write and all
   182	delete handlers fail closed.
   183	
   184	The Photon read/import boundary applies the same rule while preserving its
   185	provider owner. `@bundjil/photon/management` resolves a redacted, project-scoped
   186	credential Effect only inside an operation; encodes one owner-named request;
   187	decodes one complete status/header/body envelope; exhausts shared-user
   188	pagination; and projects phone, assigned-number, callback-query,
   189	subscription/customer, signing-secret, provider-body, and SDK data out of
   190	state-safe results. A reused bounded exponential retry policy handles only
   191	rate-limited and transient reads. `@bundjil/infrastructure/photon` consumes the
   192	decoded services and exposes retained read/import Resources whose reconcile
   193	re-observes and whose deletes fail closed.
   194	
   195	Keep each named operation flat and sequential. Keep its one-use encoding,
   196	decoding, and error mapping visible at the call site. A retry Schedule or other
   197	helper is justified only when reused or when it owns a non-trivial tested
   198	policy. Use `Match` and Effect tagged-error operators for typed branching;
   199	native-class error checks, unsafe casts, public raw causes, duplicated DTOs,
   200	and generic wrapper/helper modules are forbidden.
   201	
   202	If a third-party signature unavoidably requires a primitive, register the exact
   203	adapter symbol in `tooling/boundary-exceptions.ts`. Do not widen a public
   204	service contract or add a cast to satisfy it. Follow
   205	`.agents/skills/effect-client-wrapper/SKILL.md` when creating or reviewing the
   206	wrapper.
   207	
   208	## Effect Control Flow
   209	
   210	Primary operations should read as flat `Effect.gen` programs:
   211	
   212	```ts
   213	const program = Effect.gen(function* operationName() {
   214	  const input = yield* Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(InputSchema)(unknownInput);
   215	  const service = yield* SomeService;
   216	  return yield* service.run(input);
   217	}).pipe(Effect.withSpan("SomeService.operationName"));
   218	```
   219	
   220	Keep the success path visible. Put typed error handling in the `.pipe(...)`
   221	after the main `Effect.gen` with `Effect.catchTag`, `Effect.catchTags`,
   222	`Effect.mapError`, logging, and spans.
   223	
   224	Avoid nested `Effect.gen` blocks unless a nested program is genuinely reusable
   225	or scopes a resource. Do not add helpers whose only job is to rename one call,
   226	hide a single property access, wrap one `Effect.map`, or shorten a clear
   227	two-line operation.
   228	
   229	Runtime execution with `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runPromise`, or
   230	`ManagedRuntime` belongs at executable app, adapter, test, or CLI edges. Domain
   231	services return Effects and depend on service tags. Keep live Layer composition
   232	in `*.layer.ts` or the executable composition root rather than constructing it
   233	inside operations.
   234	
   235	Runtime time follows the same ownership rule. Read the current epoch through
   236	`Clock.currentTimeMillis`, then construct `Date` from that explicit value only
   237	at the formatting boundary. Tests of sleeps, retries, schedules, deadlines or
   238	timeouts fork the lazy Effect, use `TestClock.adjust` or `TestClock.setTime`,
   239	then join or inspect the Fiber. Fixed decoded epochs are appropriate for
   240	fixtures that merely need a valid future timestamp. Host `Date.now`, raw
   241	timers and `TestClock.withLive` are reserved for exact registered process or
   242	framework proofs; they are not a shortcut around deterministic test time.
   243	
   244	Non-cryptographic runtime identities follow the same rule. Generate them from
   245	fiber-local `Random` and prove reproducibility with `Random.withSeed`; do not
   246	call ambient `Math.random` or `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID`. Keep Web Crypto
   247	entropy only at explicit cryptographic boundaries such as PKCE material and
   248	AES-GCM IVs, where cryptographic security is the observable requirement.
   249	
   250	Choose state and collections by their observable semantics. Use one cohesive
   251	immutable Ref value only when fields share an invariant and must transition
   252	atomically. Keep independent Refs for independent observation or lifetime;
   253	use `SynchronizedRef` for serialized or effectful transitions,
   254	`SubscriptionRef` for a real subscriber stream, and `ScopedRef` for a
   255	replaceable resource. Use `Schema.NonEmptyArray` only for an at-least-one
   256	boundary, not as proof of exact cardinality. Atom is not a backend runtime
   257	state primitive.
   258	
   259	An Effect traversal callback returns its immutable observation; it does not
   260	mutate outer counters or collections that the caller later relies on. Derive
   470	model output. Any hosted or provider observation belongs in a dated,
   471	target-owned proof receipt with a source identity, `observedAt`, limitations,
   472	and non-claims. It never grants deployment or mutation authority.
   473	
   474	Channel handoff observability tests must use the decoded app contract and
   475	memory Layer to prove HMAC determinism/key separation, exact phase ordering,
   476	native Exit classification, and forbidden-marker absence. A `202`, started
   477	Fiber, registered `waitUntil`, safe fingerprint, or generated Workflow
   478	function is not a substitute for the delayed `send()` acceptance oracle.
   479	
   480	## Workflow and authority policy
   481	
   482	Workflow or provider-authority changes run the machine-readable register,
   483	action-lock, and workflow semantic gate:
   484	
   485	```bash
   486	bun run check:authority
   487	bun run check:controls
   488	bun run test:boundaries
   489	```
   490	
   491	The gate rejects missing authority-envelope fields, unavailable readback
   492	reported as healthy, tool/preflight-derived authority, secret-bearing records,
   493	unsafe emergency containment, mutable or mismatched action pins, widened
   494	permissions, target mismatch, unbounded jobs, repeated review loops,
   495	unapproved mutation, release publication, and restoration of retired automatic
   496	Claude review. It proves source desired state only. GitHub and each provider
   497	remain authoritative for current identity, settings, credentials, runs, and
   498	consequences.
   499	
   500	## Documentation Quality
   501	
   502	Every durable feature should leave behind:
   503	
   504	- a package README update when package behavior changes;
   505	- an architecture doc update when ownership or patterns change;
   506	- app README updates for commands, env vars, routes, and local proof;
   507	- a SPEC and task ledger for new apps, channels, providers, or package
   508	  boundaries.
   509	
   510	Provider package tests must exercise the supported export surface as well as
   511	internal behavior. Keep a negative export oracle when a raw transport service
   512	or byte stream must remain package-private; inspect every supported subpath,
   513	not only the root barrel. A direct proof test must reject a
   514	plausible successful transport response that lacks the semantic completion
   515	event; status, content type, byte count and line count are insufficient proof.
   516	Secret-negative telemetry tests capture the structured logger payload and

content.text:
**Findings**

1. **[P1] The proxy service lets its caller choose both the presented bearer and the expected secret.**  
   [contracts.ts:573](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/contracts.ts:573) places `authorization` and `internalToken` in the same operation input; [openai-compatible-proxy.ts:37](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/openai-compatible-proxy.ts:37) compares those caller-supplied values. Any in-process consumer can submit `Bearer x` and token `x` and pass authentication. The authorization header is also an unbounded plain string and comparison is not constant-time. This violates the stable-dependency and secret-boundary rules in [strict-effect-ts:122](/Users/cooper/.agents/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md:122).  
   **Correction:** capture the expected redacted token when constructing the service Layer. The operation should accept only a bounded, branded, redacted presented credential plus completion data, using constant-time comparison.  
   **Oracle:** directly call the service with an attacker-selected credential and prove the caller cannot replace the expected token; cover correct, incorrect, malformed and secret-negative error/log cases.

2. **[P1] Repeated provider output indexes can emit duplicate tool calls.**  
   [stream-mapper.ts:110](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/stream-mapper.ts:110) unconditionally assigns a new OpenAI tool index, while [stream-mapper.ts:116](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/stream-mapper.ts:116) overwrites an existing `output_index`. Two sequential `response.output_item.added` events with the same provider index therefore produce two downstream tool calls. An agent could execute the same external action twice despite valid `sequence_number` progression. This violates the ordered streaming invariant in [testing-and-quality.md:536](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md:536).  
   **Correction:** make output-item index uniqueness part of the shared stream state and fail before overwriting an existing index.  
   **Oracle:** send two added events with distinct sequence numbers but the same `output_index`; require a typed stream failure, no second tool-call chunk, finish reason, or `[DONE]`.

3. **[P2] Decoded function parameters retain caller-owned mutable objects.**  
   [contracts.ts:228](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/contracts.ts:228) uses `Schema.declare`, which validates and returns the original object. A read-only probe decoded `{safe:true}`, mutated the original afterward, and the subsequent Schema encoding emitted `{"safe":true,"injected":"changed-after-decode"}`.
